set.body: Backfill every doc with its stable identity key and a current-vs-historical state. Frozen docs (plans, snapshots, old reports) are never edited — their metadata goes in sidecar files; only sanctioned living docs get in-place frontmatter. After this, every page can say what it is and whether it is current. set.body: Nightly log compaction has failed for three nights, so old events are not being archived. Cause: a work item id was mistyped once, creating a ghost item with no creation record; when the compactor snapshots it, it fills in default fields the original never had, notices the result differs, and aborts to be safe. Fix: the compactor must write the item exactly as folded — defaults belong at creation time, not snapshot time — plus a regression test covering a closed ghost item.

set.body: Rick's downstream harness_engineering_book repo hit a real bug: plan-capture's overwrite guard checked only today's UTC-dated filename, so a plan authored in local evening time (behind UTC) silently duplicated with tomorrow's date. Fix: glob by slug across all dates instead of one filename.
set.resolution: Merged upstream via PR #198 (amended to reference this item). Fixes plan-capture's date-based false-negative duplicate bug plus the missing Code-Walkthrough Home link.
set.title: Fix plan-capture slug-scoped duplicate guard (PR #198)

set.body: docs/plans/*-<slug>.md matches by raw suffix, not by field boundary: searching for slug 'migration' also matches an existing 2026-07-01-database-migration.md (slug 'database-migration'), since that filename also ends in '-migration.md'. This would wrongly refuse a legitimately new, different slug. Found during review of PR #198 before merging it upstream.
set.resolution: Fixed and merged via PR #198: anchored the slug guard on the YYYY-MM-DD date field boundary instead of a bare suffix glob, with a regression test.
set.title: Glob boundary bug in the new slug guard causes false-positive refusal

set.body: worklog close and worklog update look up the item by exact dict key (fold(...).items.get(a.item) / base(a.item, ...)) instead of resolving prefixes the way worklog reopen already does (id.startswith(a.item)). Passing an 8-char prefix — the normal form worklog show/list output and the docs recommend — silently writes a new orphan phantom item under the short id instead of erroring or resolving to the real item; on update it also skips taxonomy validation since the current-state lookup silently returns {}. Reproduced live: 'worklog close 01KYA8MD' (valid prefix of 01KYA8MDY5HP9MC5KQMJX3BN84) created an orphan closed item instead of closing the real one. Fix: give close/update the same prefix-resolution + not-found error that reopen already has.
set.resolution: close/update/link now resolve id prefixes via a shared _resolve(); ambiguous prefixes error instead of picking arbitrarily. Regression tests in tests/test_resolve.py
set.title: close/update silently corrupt log when given an item-id prefix instead of the full ULID

set.body: bin/sync_dispatch.py push_items(): the scope skip ('closed and not ext.get("key") and not forced: continue') is correctly bypassed when --keys forces the item in, but the closed-item branch unconditionally reads ext['key'] (both the dry-run print and the real close() call), assuming a closed item always already has an external key. A closed item that was NEVER pushed (no external.key) and is forced into scope via --keys crashes with KeyError: 'key' instead of create-then-close. Repro: bin/worklog sync --dry-run --keys <ulid-of-closed-never-remote-item>. Hit while reconciling 01KYAH3VHPSEK2RY63J7Y109FR (release item, done, never remote) during v0.14.0 wiki/ticket publish; worked around by manually running the adapter's create step + worklog link before syncing, so the item enters the already-working closed+ext.key path. Fix: in the closed branch, if not ext.get('key'), do create-then-close (mirror the non-closed create path) instead of assuming update-then-close.
set.resolution: Fixed in commit fb801f1, shipped via PR #188 (v0.16.0): closed branch now does create-then-close when a never-pushed closed item is forced into scope via --keys. Regression test: tests/test_dispatch.py::TestCloseNeverPushed.
set.title: sync_dispatch push_items KeyError on ext['key'] when forcing a never-remote closed item into scope via --keys

set.body: After v0.17.0 shipped, a sweep of the work log against the actual repo found four items that no longer match reality — a closed-out release still marked open, a finished epic still open and therefore invisible on the roadmap, a session health check that cries wolf on every start, and two abandoned worktrees. It also turned up hard evidence that a known bug has already corrupted this repo's own work log: closing an item by the short id the tool prints creates a phantom item instead. This plan clears the drift and fixes that bug at its root.

set.body:
The session-start health check compares the configured git hooks path
against the literal string "hooks", so a repo wired with the full absolute
path — the form that actually works inside a git worktree — is reported as
broken every session. Widen the check to accept any path that resolves to
the repo's own hooks directory, in the session hook, its plugin mirror, and
the doctor command.
set.resolution: doctor and doctor-lite accept any core.hooksPath resolving to this repo's hooks/, not just the literal 'hooks'
set.title: Accept an absolute core.hooksPath in the doctor checks

set.body:

through it, and error clearly when a short id matches more than one item.
